ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC = 5$, $BC = 12$. Let $D$ be a moving point on $AB$. Construct $DE \perp AC$ at point $E$ and $DF \perp BC$ at point $F$. Connect $EF$. What is the minimum value of the line segment $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect CD.\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, AC = 5, BC = 12,\\
$\therefore$ AB = $\sqrt{AC^2 + BC^2}$ = $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2}$ = 13,\\
$\because$ DE $\perp$ AC, DF $\perp$ BC, $\angle C = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral CFDE is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ EF = CD,\\
By the principle that the perpendicular segment is the shortest, when CD $\perp$ AB, the value of segment EF is the smallest,\\
At this moment, $S_{\triangle ABC} = \frac{1}{2} \text{BC} \cdot \text{AC} = \frac{1}{2} \text{AB} \cdot \text{CD}$,\\
which means $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 13 \cdot \text{CD}$,\\
Solving yields: CD = $\frac{60}{13}$,\\
$\therefore$ EF = $\boxed{\frac{60}{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower right, AC is vertical and CB is horizontal, so ∠ACB is a right angle. Point D is located on the hypotenuse AB; from D draw a perpendicular to AC, meeting AC at E, and in the figure DE is a horizontal line; from D draw a perpendicular to BC, meeting BC at F, and in the figure DF is a vertical line; EF is connected. It can be seen from the figure that C, F, D, E form a rectangle. Reasoning: Because AC=5, BC=12, and ∠ACB=90°, so AB=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13. Since DE⊥AC, DF⊥BC, and AC⊥BC, quadrilateral CFDE is a rectangle. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, therefore EF=CD. Thus to make EF minimal, it is equivalent to making CD minimal when D is on AB. The shortest distance from a point to a line is the perpendicular segment, so when CD⊥AB, CD takes the minimum value. At this time CD is the altitude from C to the hypotenuse AB. Calculate using the area of the triangle: S△ABC=(1/2)·AC·BC=(1/2)·5·12=30; at the same time S△ABC=(1/2)·AB·CD=(1/2)·13·CD. Therefore 30=(13/2)CD, solving gives CD=60/13. Because EF=CD, the minimum value of EF is 60/13.
